correctness.rationale: Derive conservative stage and final Patankar solve for x and v. Substitution yields the rational multiplier m_t(D), whose strictly positive denominator and strictly negative derivative make the two endpoint values exhaustive. Their strict -1-to-1 bounds prove global contraction; monotone crossing yields the unique minimax root; the boundary sign and t=2 substitution establish both sharpness and cubic order. The standalone verifier checks exact rational steps and identities, while infinite-domain conclusions use the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Examined original definitions and stability analyses (arXiv:1702.04589, 2202.01099 and 2309.01562) and compared their logical conclusions with the exact globally quantified contraction, sharp best step, noncrossing boundary and cubic recursion. The 2022 paper proves local two-way stability and one-way global decay; neither entails a global two-way nonlinear multiplier. Relevant targeted mathematical-record queries produced no result covering all claims. The remaining publication-priority uncertainty is reported.
residual_risks: A specialized article may independently derive the same symmetric closed scalar map and its extrema without using searched aliases.

value.rationale: The originating global-versus-local MPRK stability literature explicitly motivates verifying global convergence with nonnegative RK parameters. A theorem giving the sharp global nonlinear contraction for the canonical strictly positive two-way exchange, the fastest worst-case step, a sharp overshoot frontier and an exceptional cubic step separates exact stability from monotone relaxation and supplies a meaningful reproducible numerical benchmark; it does not claim all-system generality.
